thread:
maria: Heads-up — multiple customers in EU reported degraded latency and unexpected billing for hosted pool traffic. They have Dedicated EU capacity but traffic is getting routed to hosted us-east-1 intermittently. Repro steps & logs below. :rotating_light:

routing-bot: [auto] New alert: tenant-983 egress -> hosted pool spike (count=78, window=5m)

sam: Oof, saw spike on telemetry too. Any recent deploys to the pinning service?

maria: Not that I know of. Repro I ran: curl -> gateway with tenant header, got 307 -> hosted and higher p95. Example: 
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Tenant: tenant-983" -H "X-Region: eu-west-1" https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
x-routing-pool: hosted-us-east-1
x-route-trace: r-20260305-tn983-abc123
```

kevin: That x-route-trace looks useful. Can you paste the trace logs r-20260305-tn983-abc123 from routing-service?

maria: Pasting filtered trace (timestamps truncated):
```
[routing-service] 2026-03-05T12:03:21Z lookup: tenant=tenant-983 -> pinned_pool=eu-dedicated-42 (ttl=0)
[routing-service] 2026-03-05T12:03:21Z pin-check: found pin timestamp=2026-03-01T08:00:00Z
[routing-service] 2026-03-05T12:03:21Z pin-ttl: computed remaining=-4h -> treat as expired
[routing-service] 2026-03-05T12:03:21Z fallback-policy: routed_to=hosted-us-east-1 reason=pin_expired
```

alex: Hmm ttl negative. Pin timestamp stale even though the Dedicated pool is healthy. Could be that the TTL refresh job failed to update pins during a scaling event.

julia: I repro'd locally by stopping the pin-refresh cron for ~2m and sending traffic. Same behavior. Looks like routing logic treats missing refresh as immediate expiry instead of grace window.

kevin: Confirmed we had a brief restart of dedicated-controller on 2026-03-01 08:00Z (autoscaler churn). There was an error in the controller that prevented the TTL touch: 
```
ERROR controller: failed to write pin meta: write timeout to registry (context deadline exceeded)
```

sam: That matches. If the controller didn't persist the heartbeat, routing treats pin as expired and falls back. But why would we observe intermittent routing (some requests hit dedicated, some hosted)?

maria: Telemetry shows a race: nodes that had an in-memory cache still consider tenant pinned for ~30-90s; new requests hitting fresh routing instances that read registry see expired pin and go to hosted. So we get partial spillover and billing noise.

billing-bot: [auto] Tenants affected: tenant-983, tenant-204, tenant-411. Preliminary hosted billing delta: +12% for eu region during window.

kevin: Action plan: 1) run pinned cleanup/invalidate script for affected tenants to force a consistent state, 2) add temporary grace window in routing, 3) fix controller write timeout PR. Assigning.

kevin: @sam can you run the cleanup script now for tenant-983 and tenant-204? Script: 
```
./tools/clear_tenant_pins --tenants tenant-983,tenant-204 --dry-run=false
```

sam: Running now. Will post outcomes.

[30s later]

sam: Done. Script output: "cleared pins: tenant-983 -> success, tenant-204 -> success". Re-ran the curl from eu node and got x-routing-pool: eu-dedicated-42 consistently. p95 back to normal.

maria: Nice. For the code fix: we should change routing to accept a small grace period (configurable, default 2m) if registry write was recently observed but pin record missing. That avoids immediate flip to hosted on transient controller failures.

alex: Agreed. Also add an observability metric: pin_heartbeat_write_failures and a small alert when >2 failures/min for a pool.

kevin: I'll open a PR with: (a) grace window, (b) metric, (c) defensive log with tenant id when fallback occurs due to pin expiry.

kevin: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/478 (draft) — includes unit tests and integration test that simulates controller restart.

julia: Two follow-ups for SRE: 1) run a one-off job to scan registry for pins with timestamp < now-1d and cross-check pool health, 2) add a runbook step to not auto-clear pins unless confirmed with tenant.

maria: Billing help: @billing-bot can you provide rollback credits for tenants with unexpected hosted charges during the window? They saw higher invoice rows.

billing-bot: Opening support tickets for each tenant and flagging finance. Ref IDs: FB-2026-8213, FB-2026-8214, FB-2026-8215. Please CC finance@redwood if anything urgent.

sam: Notes for repro doc: 1) stop pin-refresh on controller, 2) send steady traffic with X-Tenant header, 3) observe mixed routing due to cache divergence, 4) run clear_tenant_pins to restore. I can draft a short KB article.

maria: Please do. Also record the exact controller exception and timeframe in the incident tracker. Assigning to @maria to follow up with tenant support for remediation and credits.

kevin: I'll merge the PR after one more review and deploy hotfix to staging. Plan deploy to prod in 2 hours if metrics look good.

maria: Thanks team. If anyone sees new tenants flapping, ping this thread and I'll escalate.
